event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
blurb:
Shakespeare meets Elvis. It's a weirder combination than it sounds, and it completely works.

All Shook Up is loosely based on Twelfth Night, set in 1955, built around a guitar-playing stranger who rides into a buttoned-up small town and shakes everything loose. The catalogue does the heavy lifting: "Heartbreak Hotel," "Hound Dog," "Jailhouse Rock," "Don't Be Cruel." You know every song before the curtain goes up. The Marietta Theatre Company is a genuine community theater with serious production chops, and this is the kind of musical that plays to a packed house for good reason.

It's rated PG, which means it works for older kids and adults equally well. A solid option if you want a real night out at the theater without driving into the city.
scoring_notes: Good fit for the mixed family and adult audience in the Perimeter. Elvis nostalgia works across age groups. Community theater is a slightly lower uniqueness ceiling than a professional touring production, but the Shakespeare connection and strong catalogue give it genuine appeal. PG rating broadens the family applicability.

blurb:
Zootopia 2 hits the outdoor screen at Pernoshal Park on Friday night, and the whole setup is genuinely hard to beat for a late-summer family evening.

Discover Dunwoody's Pics in the Park series is free admission, free popcorn, free candy, and giveaways. The popcorn cart opens before the film so you can get settled on the lawn before the movie starts at 9. It's Dunwoody, it's walkable for a lot of Perimeter families, and Zootopia 2 is exactly the kind of movie that works just as well for the adults as it does for the kids.

No tickets, no fuss. Pack a blanket, show up early to grab your spot, and let the night handle the rest.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the young families segment of the Perimeter audience. Free admission is a nice bonus even for a $105K household. Hyperlocal to Dunwoody, which is core Perimeter territory. Uniqueness is moderate since it's part of a series, but Zootopia 2 is a new release that adds some freshness.

blurb:
If you grew up with Bon Jovi on the radio and Michael Jackson on the TV, this one is going to hit different.

SPANKthe80s has been doing this since 1999, which means they've had a long time to get really, really good at it. This isn't a cover band running through the obvious tracks. It's a full visual production with the costumes, the lights, and the between-song energy to actually transport you back. Two full sets at the Strand Theatre in Marietta, wrapping up around 9.

The median age of the Perimeter audience is right in the sweet spot for peak 80s nostalgia. Round up a group of people you'd dance in public with and make it a Thursday worth remembering.
scoring_notes: Strong audience match for the 35-45 demographic that makes up a big portion of the Perimeter readership. 80s nostalgia is a reliable draw for this income and age bracket. Uniqueness is moderate since SPANKthe80s tours regularly, but a local performance at a premium theater still clears the bar for a featured mention.

event_name: Joe Gransden's The Good Life: The Artistry of Tony Bennett
blurb:
Tony Bennett would have turned 100 this year. Joe Gransden is throwing the kind of tribute that actually honors that.

This isn't a generic tribute show with a setlist of obvious hits. Gransden walks you through Bennett's life and career as one of the defining voices of the American Songbook, weaving in music from Sinatra, Louis Armstrong, Dean Martin, and the others who shaped who Tony was. It's a real concert with real context, and if you have any connection to that era of music, you're going to feel it.

The VIP experience is worth considering: early seating, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet with the band, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. The Strand is a beautiful room for this. Grab tickets before the weekend fills up.
scoring_notes: The centennial hook gives this show a legitimate reason to exist and attend. Adult skew is strong, which matches the Perimeter audience profile. The Strand is a premium small venue experience that appeals to the educated, higher-income demographic. Empty nesters in particular will find this compelling.

event_name: Billy Currington & Kip Moore at Coca-Cola Roxy
blurb:
Two heavy hitters on one stage, one night only. That's a good deal by any measure.

Billy Currington and Kip Moore are both coming to Coca-Cola Roxy on August 8th, and if you've been waiting for an excuse to make a night of it at The Battery, this is a pretty good one. Currington is one of those artists who has an unfair number of songs you already know by heart. Moore brings a rawer, road-worn energy that plays great live. Together they're going to make a Saturday night feel like a Saturday night.

The Roxy is an outstanding venue for this kind of show. Good sightlines, great sound, and everything The Battery offers before and after means you can make it a full evening. Tickets won't last forever on this one.
scoring_notes: Country music skews well for this demographic. The Battery is convenient for Perimeter residents and the dual-headliner format adds value. Not an ultra-rare show but a legitimate concert night from two established artists at a great venue. Strong fit for young professionals and couples.

event_name: Gipsy Kings at Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
Twenty million albums sold. A Grammy for Best World Music. And a catalogue that has somehow found its way into every good party, every great restaurant, and every road trip playlist that mattered. The Gipsy Kings don't need an introduction. They need a date on your calendar.

They're coming to Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre on August 13th, and this is the kind of show that sounds completely different live than it does through speakers. The flamenco-driven rhythm, the layered vocals, the sheer physicality of how this band plays, you feel it in the room in a way that a recording just can't replicate.

Cobb Energy is a beautiful venue, easy to get to from the Perimeter, and the crowd at a Gipsy Kings show is always a good one. Check the box office for ticket availability and don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: Strong demographic fit. The Gipsy Kings appeal broadly across the 35-55 age range and the educated, culturally curious Perimeter audience. World music at a performing arts center skews adult, which matches this newsletter's profile. Grammy-winning legacy act adds legitimacy and uniqueness.

event_name: Grateful Dead Meet-Up at the Movies 2026
blurb:
This is not a tribute band. This is not a documentary. This is the actual show, on the big screen, in surround sound, with a room full of people who have been waiting for exactly this.

The 2026 Grateful Dead Meet-Up at the Movies brings the complete June 17, 1991 concert from Giants Stadium back to theaters for one screening only. It's considered one of the greatest shows of the band's final decade, captured on 48-track tape and remixed in full surround sound by Jeffrey Norman. You get "Eyes of the World" opening the set, six separate "Dark Star" teases building through the night before the full song finally explodes, and the whole thing wrapping up with the band covering "The Weight." It is a REMARKABLE setlist.

SpringsCinema is right in your backyard and it's a taphouse, so you're not exactly watching this in a regular movie theater. Grab tickets before the Deadheads buy them all.
scoring_notes: Extremely high uniqueness score. One screening only, 35th anniversary, at a local taphouse cinema in Sandy Springs. The Grateful Dead skews toward the 38-55 demographic which is well represented in this audience. Not a universal fit but the can't-miss factor and hyperlocal venue make it a strong candidate.

blurb:
There are not a lot of nights where the setting does as much work as the music. This is one of them.

Sunset Sips brings the Georgia Symphony Orchestra's jazz ensemble out to the Great Lawn at Chattahoochee Nature Center for an evening of live jazz as the sun goes down over the river. Sam Skelton leads the band through the real stuff, the swinging, soulful, big-sound jazz that actually makes you stop mid-conversation and just listen. You're outside, drink in hand, surrounded by nature, watching the sky change colors. It's genuinely hard to do better than that on a Thursday night.

This is an adult night out that doesn't need a lot of explanation. Grab someone worth sitting next to on a lawn, show up around 6, and let the evening do the rest.
scoring_notes: Perfect fit for the Perimeter audience's adult skew and $105K income level. Outdoor jazz at a nature center hits the young professional and empty nester segments equally well. Not a weekly recurring event, and the GSO jazz format gives it a legitimacy that casual cover band nights don't have. Strong on all four factors.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
price: Varies (check festival for individual screening prices and passes)
blurb:
The Cobb International Film Festival is back at the Strand on Marietta Square, and for anyone who wants more from a movie than what's playing at the multiplex right now, this is it.

Films from 20-plus countries, across drama, documentary, and short form. A lot of the screenings include live Q&A with the filmmakers, which changes the experience entirely. You're not just watching a film and driving home. You're sitting in a conversation about how it got made, what the filmmaker was trying to say, and what it actually means. That's the part you won't get on streaming in November.

Festival passes are available, and Vet Tix is a partner, meaning if you know someone who has served, full festival passes are available to them through that program. The festival runs into the following week, so you've got time to browse the screening schedule and pick something that sounds genuinely interesting. Go to the Strand website, pull up the lineup, and find something that makes you a little curious.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the 65% college-educated demographic that responds to international and documentary content. The filmmaker Q&A element adds real uniqueness. Marietta Square location is hyperlocal. Multi-day festival means readers have multiple entry points. Annual event but each year's lineup is new. Good fit for curious, well-traveled empty nesters and couples who want more than mainstream entertainment.

event_name: All Shook Up: The Elvis Presley Musical
venue: Marietta's Theatre in the Square, Marietta
blurb:
Elvis Presley meets Shakespeare at Theatre in the Square, and somehow it works completely.

All Shook Up is a jukebox musical set in 1955 built entirely around Elvis's greatest hits, running the story of a leather-jacketed stranger who rolls into a repressed Midwestern town and turns everything upside down. The structure is borrowed from Twelfth Night, which sounds like a stretch until you're actually in the theater laughing and wondering how you didn't see that coming.

Multiple weekends, multiple showtimes, so you've got options. Matinees on the 15th, 16th, and 22nd if Sunday afternoon suits you better than a weeknight. It's right here in Marietta, the kind of local theater production that this community actually shows up for. If it's been a while since you've been to Theatre in the Square, this is a good reason to go back.
scoring_notes: Elvis catalog resonates with the 42+ median age audience. Shakespeare-based plot adds an intellectual hook that fits the 65% college-educated demographic. Multi-weekend run gives flexibility, which increases attendance likelihood. Theatre in the Square is hyperlocal and beloved. Good fit for couples, established families with older teens, and empty nesters looking for a real night out.

blurb:
This one is a little different from just going to a Braves game, and that's the point.

Bats and Bites is an early-access experience at Truist Park where you get a guided tour of the stadium, end up in the Outfield Market, sample new featured food and a signature beer or cocktail, meet a former Braves player, and then watch batting practice from the outfield. You might even catch a ball.

For anyone who has been to Truist a hundred times and feels like they've seen it, this is the version that gets you somewhere the regular ticket doesn't. The food angle, the former player meet, and batting practice access together make it a genuinely different afternoon than your standard Friday night game. Great for a date, great with a couple of friends, great if you've got a teenager who would absolutely lose it standing in the outfield watching BP. Grab your spot before it fills up.
scoring_notes: East Cobb is Braves country. This audience has high affinity for Truist Park but this experience goes beyond a standard game ticket. The food-forward, behind-the-scenes format appeals to established families (teens would love batting practice access) and couples alike. $118K median income means ticket cost is not a barrier. Unique enough to stand out from a standard game day.

event_name: Derek Hough: Symphony of Dance Encore
venue: Cobb Energy Performing Arts Centre, Atlanta
blurb:
If you've ever watched Dancing With the Stars and thought the live version must be something else entirely, this is your chance to find out.

Derek Hough brings his Symphony of Dance: Encore tour to Cobb Energy on August 8. This is a full production, not a dance competition recap or a meet-and-greet with a velvet rope. We're talking ballroom, tap, salsa, hip-hop, and contemporary all wrapped into one show with lighting, costumes, and stage design built to make your jaw drop. Derek choreographed and stars in it himself, which means the level of craft on that stage is the REAL deal.

It's right here in Cobb County, which means no downtown parking nightmare and no long drive. Just a polished, high-energy night out that's genuinely different from anything else on the calendar this month. Grab your tickets before the good seats disappear.
scoring_notes: Strong pull for the 40s-and-up female demographic and couples looking for a real night out. Derek Hough has mainstream name recognition from DWTS. Cobb Energy is local and familiar. Not a recurring event, one-night-only at this venue. Ticket price is not an issue for a $118K median income household. Good fit for empty nesters and couples.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
If you were alive and paying attention in the 80s, this show is going to do something to you.

SPANKthe80s has been doing this since 1999 and they are not messing around. Michael Jackson. Prince. Bon Jovi. Journey. The light show, the hair, the fashion, the full sensory overload that made that decade what it was. This isn't a cover band halfheartedly running through Power of Love in a bar. It's a two-set production at the Strand with a real stage, real costumes, and a crowd that already knows every word.

The median age of this neighborhood is 42. Do the math. This is squarely aimed at the people who had these songs on cassette tape and consider this era their era. It's a Thursday night, which means the weekend starts early if you want it to. Lobby opens at 6:30 if you want to get settled in. Showtime is 7:30.
scoring_notes: The 42 median age means this audience was 14-18 during the peak 80s era. Direct nostalgia hit. The Strand is local and familiar. Two-set production at a real theater elevates it above a typical bar cover band. Strong empty nester and couples night appeal. Thursday date is slightly off but still viable for a newsletter that publishes this week.

event_name: Joe Gransden's The Good Life: The Artistry of Tony Bennett
venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
Tony Bennett would have turned 100 this year. Joe Gransden is throwing him a proper birthday party at the Strand, and you're invited.

Joe and his band will walk you through Bennett's life and career, from the standards he made famous to the friends and mentors who shaped him, including Sinatra, Louis Armstrong, and Dean Martin. Two full sets with an intermission. This isn't background music at a dinner party. It's a real show, built around one of the greatest voices the American Songbook ever produced.

The VIP experience is worth a hard look. Early access seating, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet with the band, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. For a Friday night on the Marietta Square, that's a pretty complete package. Buy tickets now, get dinner on the Square before the show, and make a full night of it.
scoring_notes: Tony Bennett's catalog resonates strongly with the 42+ median age crowd, and the 100th birthday angle makes this a one-time event, not just another jazz show. The Strand is a beloved local venue. VIP tier appeals to the $118K income household that wants the full experience. Strong empty nester appeal. The Marietta Square location adds a dinner-and-a-show dynamic that this audience loves.

event_name: Glover Park Concert Series: Seven Bridges (Eagles Tribute)
price: Free (reserved tables available for a fee)
blurb:
This Friday night, Glover Park on the Marietta Square turns into an outdoor Eagles concert. Seven Bridges plays the tribute slot in the 2026 Glover Park Concert Series, and if you've ever sat in a car with the windows down and let Hotel California run all the way through, you already know this is your night.

The Series is FREE to attend, which for a summer Friday in a walkable square surrounded by restaurants and bars is honestly hard to beat. Bring a chair, grab dinner first at one of the Square spots, and settle in. If you want an actual table up front, those are available for a fee but they sell out fast, so don't wait.

This is exactly the kind of low-effort, high-payoff summer night that East Cobb was built for. Show up, kick back, and let Don Henley do the rest.
scoring_notes: Eagles tribute is a direct hit for the 42-median-age audience who grew up on classic rock. Free admission removes all friction. Marietta Square is hyperlocal and walkable. The concert series is recurring monthly but each act is unique, and an Eagles tribute on a Friday night in late July is a genuinely strong draw for this crowd. Established families and empty nesters both show up for this format.

event_name: Jazz at The Strand: The Music of Dave Brubeck
blurb:
If you've ever had "Take Five" come on and just... stopped whatever you were doing, this one's for you.

The Jazz Legacy Project is bringing a full tribute to Dave Brubeck to the Strand on Sunday afternoon. Brubeck's "Time Out" is one of the best-selling jazz albums in history, and this show works through that iconic record while weaving in the story of the bold stances Brubeck took during the Civil Rights movement. It's not just a concert. It's a real piece of American music history, live on stage, ten minutes from your driveway.

The format is clean: one act, no intermission, done by 5:30. VIP guests get an early experience starting at 2:30 PM. General admission doors open at 3:00 PM with seating at 3:30.

A Sunday afternoon at the Strand with Brubeck playing? That's a genuinely hard thing to pass up.
scoring_notes: This audience skews 42 median age with high income and education. Dave Brubeck's 'Time Out' era is deeply familiar to this demographic. The Strand is a beloved local venue. Sunday afternoon timing is ideal for established families and empty nesters. The Civil Rights history angle adds substance beyond a typical concert. High uniqueness because this is a curated, one-afternoon ticketed show, not a recurring series night.
